papers.title: The Sleep-Wake Classification Performance of Pediatric-Trained Machine Learning Algorithms for Raw Accelerometer Data.
papers.summary: Trained eight pediatric sleep-wake machine-learning classifiers on raw wrist accelerometer data from 65 children with polysomnography; the local-global LSTM achieved the best epoch-by-epoch performance (balanced accuracy 0.85, sensitivity 0.88, specificity 0.83, ROC-AUC 0.95, kappa 0.67), exceeding an adult-trained random forest and GGIR algorithms, and underestimated sleep duration by a mean 25 minutes without proportional bias.

papers.title: Partial lesions of hypocretin neurons of the rat lateral hypothalamus affect wake and sleep regulation under increased sleep pressure
papers.summary: In rats with partial (~30%) lesions of lateral hypothalamic hypocretin neurons, normal sleep-wake patterns were unchanged, but after 6 h sleep deprivation lesions accelerated compensatory slow-wave sleep dynamics and slightly reduced theta frequency during wakefulness and REM sleep.

papers.title: Cross-Band Coupling of EEG Infraslow Oscillations during NREM Sleep in Mice.
papers.summary: Analyzed cross-band coupling of EEG infraslow oscillations (0.01-0.03 Hz) across six frequency bands during NREM sleep in mice, finding that alpha, sigma, beta, and theta ISOs form a strongly correlated and phase-locked motif replicated in wild-type and LepR-Cre transgenic mice, while gamma coupling was moderate and delta was uncorrelated or absent.

papers.title: Advancing Pediatric Sleep Assessment through Spectral Sleep Scoring: A Comparison with Polysomnography.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Validated a spectral sleep-scoring approach against AASM visual scoring in 192 children aged 9-18 years, reporting high agreement between visual and spectral stages (71-89%, Cohen's kappa = 0.76) and proposing spectral scoring as an efficient pediatric method capturing additional clinically relevant sleep physiology.

papers.title: Using wearable EEG to examine age trends in sleep macro- and micro-architecture across adolescence.
papers.summary: Tested the Dreem3 sleep EEG headband for replicating established age effects in sleep physiology in 100 typically developing youth aged 9-26 years across 3-4 at-home nights. Dreem3 reproduced known age trends, including increases in NREM stage 2% and decreases in N3%, time in bed, and NREM delta and theta power, while exploratory analyses found decreased spindle activity with age.

papers.title: Reduced-observable dynamic mode decomposition for identifying theta and beta activity in working-memory EEG
papers.summary: Introduces Reduced-Observable Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (RO-eDMD) with a Random Fourier Features dictionary to extract transient theta and beta oscillatory power from multichannel working-memory EEG. Using the extracted theta power in a logistic regression, the authors report correlations with encoding events and memory load, replicating prior findings, in a computationally efficient Koopman-based framework.

papers.title: CADENCE: Open-source software for signal conditioning, feature extraction, visualization and analysis of cardiac optical mapping data.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Developed CADENCE, an open-source MATLAB-based pipeline for cardiac optical mapping that combines signal conditioning, feature extraction, and analysis in an end-to-end application. CADENCE was validated across four species and multiple tissue and camera configurations, showing agreement with blinded experts comparable to inter-observer variability and median dominant frequency error of 0.03%.

papers.title: Channel-Adaptive Temporal Modeling with Grouped Convolutional Network and Informer for Seizure Detection and Prediction.
papers.summary: Proposed GCNN-Informer, a channel-adaptive deep learning framework combining grouped convolutional networks, CBAM attention, and a lightweight Informer encoder for multi-channel EEG seizure detection and prediction. On the CHB-MIT dataset under patient-specific evaluation, it achieved 97.33% detection accuracy and 97.28% prediction accuracy with low false rates (0.30/h and 0.03/h).

papers.title: A Personalized Approach to Student Mental Health: Real-Time EEG Biofeedback for Stress and Focus Management
papers.summary: Investigated a subject-specific thresholding approach for student stress and focus monitoring using a two-channel EEG setup and ESP32-based FFT pipeline, comparing Beta/Alpha and Theta/Alpha ratios across Baseline, Focused, and Stressed task conditions. Pilot descriptive results showed Beta/Alpha rising from 2.76 (Baseline) to 2.88 (Stressed) and Theta/Alpha lowest in Focused (0.95) and highest in Stressed (1.04), but classification accuracy, significance, and generalization were not established.

papers.title: Longitudinal Imaging in a Mouse Model of Focal Cortical Dysplasia Reveals Lesion Expansion and Loss of Pre-Discharge Neuronal Recruitment
papers.summary: Combined chronic two-photon calcium imaging through a cranial window with video-EEG in an in utero electroporation mouse model of focal cortical dysplasia type II carrying the mTOR p.L2427P variant. The lesion progressively expanded in adulthood (partly via dysmorphic neuron somatic growth), and in seizing mice dysmorphic and pyramidal neuron activity declined while reliable pre-interictal-discharge neuronal recruitment present in non-seizing cortex was lost at late stages.

papers.title: Lifespan Trajectories of Resting State Bipolar EEG Power.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Derived lifespan trajectories of resting-state bipolar EEG power from 12,906 observations in 5,781 participants aged 12-70 without alcohol use disorder, analyzing seven frequency bands and 24 bipolar channels. EEG power decreased sharply from age 12 to the early 20s, followed by divergent patterns including increases in beta frequencies and mixed theta/alpha changes, with striking sex differences in inter-frequency correlation trajectories.

papers.title: Phase-dependent EEG decoding of continuous visual stimuli.
papers.summary: Recorded EEG while participants viewed 2-s Gabor patches and applied phase-dependent decoding to test whether alpha phase modulates visual representation strength. Decoding accuracy varied systematically with alpha phase in a unimodal profile peaking over occipito-parietal electrodes, indicating more accurate visual representation at specific alpha phases during continuous input.

papers.title: Transcranial Evoked Potentials are Minimally Influenced by Afferent Feedback From Peripheral Muscle Contraction.
papers.summary: Combined M1 TMS-EEG with electromyography, accelerometry, and peripheral electrical stimulation to dissociate central from peripheral contributions to TMS-evoked potentials. Larger motor outputs covaried with distinct EEG morphologies across all time windows including pre-feedback latencies, whereas isolated muscle contraction produced only delayed (>65 ms) small responses, indicating TMS-evoked potentials mainly reflect baseline motor cortex excitability.

papers.title: Multimodal evidence associated with 20Hz rTMS in AD: neuroaxonal injury reduction, neural oscillatory rebalancing, and multilayer network integration.
papers.summary: Combined a randomized sham-controlled rTMS trial in 16 AD patients with a single-arm multimodal cohort of 30 patients; active DLPFC rTMS improved MMSE and MoCA, while cohort analyses showed decreased NfL, altered delta/beta/gamma power, and reduced modularity with enhanced global efficiency across theta, alpha, and beta bands. MoCA improvement correlated with gamma-band global efficiency and multilayer clustering coefficients.

papers.title: A robust adversarial learning framework for EEG emotion recognition.
papers.summary: Proposed a two-stage adversarial domain generalization framework for cross-subject EEG emotion recognition, combining LSTM encoders with adversarial domain-invariant/domain-specific representation learning and distributionally robust optimization with gradient-guided feature augmentation. Under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, the method reached mean accuracies of 69.94% and 68.97% and F1 scores of 0.59 and 0.65 on AMIGOS and DREAMER, outperforming comparison methods, with adversarial learning providing the main generalization gain.

papers.title: Age and sex impact resting-state EEG aperiodic activity beyond symptom associations in persistent post-concussive symptoms
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional high-density resting-state EEG study of 70 patients with persistent post-concussive symptoms and 38 age-matched controls, aperiodic offset and exponent were extracted from power spectra and related to demographics and symptom burden. Younger age and male sex were associated with higher offset and exponent values, while no clinical or symptom variable improved model fit beyond age and sex, and no patient-control differences remained after adjustment for age and sex.

papers.title: Stability of the Epileptogenic Index across seizures and the effects of sleep and withdrawal of anti-seizure medications.
papers.summary: Analyzed 127 SEEG seizures from 19 patients to assess within-patient stability of the Epileptogenic Index and effects of vigilance state and anti-seizure medication dose. Seizure-to-seizure EI correlations ranged from 0.11 to 0.81, with no wake-sleep differences but significantly higher p_weighted EI during reduced ASM doses, suggesting ASM status should be considered when interpreting EI maps.

papers.title: A Novel Digital Phenotype of Physical Activity: Associations with Heart Rate Fragmentation.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 602 older male veterans, Gaussian mixture modeling of accelerometry across six physical activity domains identified two overlapping phenotypes (compact-early and diffuse-late). The diffuse-late phenotype was associated with higher heart rate fragmentation (PIP and IALS), linking activity timing and dispersion to neuroautonomic dysregulation.

papers.title: Design and Test Novel EEG Electrode Attachments for Type 4 Afro-textured Hairstyles.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Designed and tested three 3D-printed, hair-anchored EEG electrode attachments for Type 4a–4c Afro-textured hairstyles in 17 adults, comparing them with a conventional 16-electrode cap. The novel attachments reduced electrode-to-scalp distance, gel use, and impedance, cut electrode disconnection from 20% to 0.1%, and improved signal quality (alpha power and 1/f component) without changing comfort.

papers.title: Elevated neuronal excitability and seizure susceptibility in a mouse model of SCN2A -related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Generated and characterized a novel Scn2a-E430A mouse model of SCN2A-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, finding hippocampal pyramidal neuron hyperexcitability and enhanced CA1 long-term potentiation. Mice showed epileptiform discharges and spectral abnormalities without spontaneous generalized seizures, faster seizure generalization and greater lethality in induction assays, and improved seizure outcomes with phenytoin pretreatment.

papers.title: A behavioral and electrophysiological study on the influence of menstrual cycle, estradiol and progesterone on the social approach-avoidance behavior tendencies of women.
papers.journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology
papers.summary: Measured estradiol, progesterone, social approach-avoidance behavior, and EEG in 27 naturally cycling women across early follicular, late follicular, and mid-luteal phases. Late follicular estradiol was associated with faster approach and smaller LPP to happy faces, while mid-luteal progesterone was associated with faster approach and smaller LPP to fearful faces, indicating hormone-specific modulation of social processing efficiency.

papers.title: Vibrotactile transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) during working memory: convergent electrophysiological evidence for cortical efficiency.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Tested sensory-amplification versus cortical-efficiency hypotheses for vibrotactile taVNS during N-back working memory in 20 healthy adults (EEG, ECG, eye-tracking) and 19 epilepsy patients with intracranial monitoring. Active vtaVNS reduced scalp visual ERPs and temporal high-gamma responses versus sham, smaller visual ERPs were linked to successful 4-back encoding, and vtaVNS shifted cortical dynamics toward criticality, supporting enhanced cortical efficiency.

papers.title: Seizures induce c-fos expression in a subset of astrocytes, termed fostrocytes, that dampen subsequent seizures.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using the TRAP2 c-fos labeling system in mouse temporal lobe epilepsy models, this study identified a subset of astrocytes termed fostrocytes that show sustained c-fos expression after status epilepticus. Selective ablation of fostrocytes with Cre-dependent diphtheria toxin increased spontaneous seizure frequency, suggesting that augmenting fostrocyte activity may have anti-seizure effects.

papers.title: A screening method for aortic valve disease based on spectral analysis of a single-channel electrocardiogram using machine learning algorithms.
papers.summary: Developed machine learning models (Balanced Random Forest and XGBoost) using spectral features of single-lead ECG to screen for moderate-to-severe aortic stenosis and regurgitation in 2,503 patients. Accuracy was 0.65–0.66 for aortic stenosis, about 0.71–0.73 for aortic regurgitation, and 0.69–0.72 for significant aortic valve disease, indicating potential screening utility.

papers.title: Developmental mechanisms contributing to non-linear firing dynamics in spinal motoneurons of the postnatal mouse.
papers.summary: Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings in postnatal mouse lumbar motoneurons showed that persistent inward currents and non-linear firing hysteresis mature in parallel in fast but not slow motoneurons after hindlimb weight-bearing. Blocking NaV1.6, L-type calcium, KCNQ, KV1.2, or HCN channels revealed that multiple voltage-gated conductances beyond PICs shape sustained firing dynamics, with HCN blockade promoting self-sustained firing in fast motoneurons.

papers.title: Temporal evolution of EEG hallmarks in childhood Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 51 children with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, review of 234 sleep video-EEGs showed that slow spike-and-wave complexes emerged earlier than generalized paroxysmal fast activity (mean 8.3 vs 9.6 years). EEG hallmarks developed progressively, with full electroclinical LGS criteria met at a median age of 10.9 years despite median epilepsy onset at 1.1 years.

papers.title: How School-Based Interventions Shape the Developing Brain during 3-12 Years: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 17 empirical neuroimaging studies (8 in an exploratory meta-analysis) examined how school-based interventions relate to brain development in children aged 3–12. It reported a preliminary association with reduced amygdala activity during stress regulation and identified mechanisms including prefrontal recruitment/efficiency, limbic-prefrontal modulation, sensory-specific electrophysiological markers, and teacher-child inter-brain synchrony linked to learning outcomes.

papers.title: Axonal dysfunction precedes axonal degeneration in a mouse model of progressive parkinsonism.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Comparing dopaminergic axons in the MitoPark mouse model of Parkinsonism with age-matched controls, this study found reduced action potential-evoked calcium signals and impaired action potential propagation with altered axonal waveforms well before dopaminergic fiber loss and motor deficits. These findings define an early period of axon-specific physiological dysfunction preceding axonal degeneration.

papers.title: Deanna Protocol Ameliorates the Deficits in Human iPSC-Cortical Neurons Carrying Familial Alzheimer's Mutation.
papers.summary: Evaluated the anaplerotic Deanna Protocol in human iPSC-derived cortical neurons carrying a PSEN1 familial Alzheimer's mutation, testing mitochondrial, morphological, electrophysiological, and LTP phenotypes. DP treatment significantly ameliorated all impairments, supporting targeting cellular energy flux in AD neurodegeneration.

papers.title: A Tutorial on Automated Mass Spectral Analysis Using NucleoSpec for Compositional Assignment of Nucleic Acid-Silver Complexes and Nanoclusters.
papers.summary: Developed NucleoSpec, an open-source web platform that automates ESI-MS composition assignment for nucleic acid-silver complexes and nanoclusters, integrating charge determination, composition enumeration, and isotope-pattern matching. Benchmarking reproduced published formulas to single-proton precision (median centroid offset 0.03 m/z) for adequate signal-to-noise spectra.

papers.title: Effect of epidural spinal cord stimulation combined with personalized neurorehabilitation in chronic motor-complete spinal cord injury: study protocol for the phase II single-arm feasibility RESTORES (RESToration Of Rehabilitative function with Epidural spinal Stimulation) trial.
papers.summary: Presents the protocol for RESTORES, a phase II single-arm feasibility trial of epidural spinal cord stimulation plus 24-week personalized neurorehabilitation in 15 adults with chronic motor-complete SCI. Primary outcome is implantation safety at 6 months, with secondary motor, functional, autonomic, and neurophysiological outcomes.

papers.title: Case Report: An MDT-guided multimodal protocol for large-area stroke plateau - integrating neuromodulation with multimodal assessment.
papers.summary: Case report of a 38-year-old male with large left hemispheric infarction treated with an 8-month MDT-guided, dynamically adjusted multimodal protocol combining rTMS, iTBS, BCI-robotic training, VR, and gait-based biomechanical correction. Marked cognitive, language, and motor gains occurred alongside neuroimaging evidence suggesting trans-hemispheric reorganization.

papers.title: Implementation and early experience with tubular retractor-assisted minimally invasive parafascicular surgery for deep brain tumors.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
papers.summary: Describes early institutional experience with tubular retractor-assisted minimally invasive parafascicular surgery (tr-MIPS) for deep intra-axial tumors in six patients. Gross or near-total resection was achieved in four, five had no new postoperative deficits, and multiple adjuncts including depth-electrode EEG were feasibly integrated.

papers.title: Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in a Pacemaker-Dependent Child with Syndromic Drug-Resistant Epilepsy: A Case Report with Prospective 9-Month Follow-Up.
papers.summary: Reported a 6-year-old pacemaker-dependent boy with TAF6-related Alazami-Yuan syndrome and drug-resistant epilepsy treated with transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation over 9 months. Seizure burden decreased from 2–4 prolonged daily seizures to about two brief generalized tonic seizures weekly, with improved PedsQL-FIM scores and no cardiac, pacing, or device-related adverse events.

papers.title: Real time quantification of carbohydrates in beer wort by FTIR and neural network analysis.
papers.journal: Journal of food science and technology
papers.summary: Developed a real-time FTIR spectroscopy system combined with principal component analysis and artificial neural networks to quantify glucose, maltose, maltotriose, and dextrins during enzymatic saccharification of beer wort. The system was demonstrated to enable real-time process monitoring and control of carbohydrate concentration during mashing.

papers.title: Epilepsy as a consequence of infantile vitamin B12 deficiency: observations from a prospective cohort study and a review of the literature.
papers.summary: Prospectively followed 141 children with symptomatic infantile vitamin B12 deficiency and found that 31 of 112 followed children (28%) developed epilepsy at a median follow-up of 51 months, with epileptic spasms as the most common seizure type. Acute-phase seizures were the strongest independent predictor of later epilepsy (pooled HR 4.27), and epilepsy risk clustered within 10 months of treatment.

papers.title: Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis with psychiatric manifestations and choreiform movements: a case report and literature review.
papers.summary: Described a 52-year-old woman with neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis presenting with psychiatric disturbances and choreiform movements, whose seizures and movement disorder improved after methylprednisolone, IVIG, plasma exchange, and subsequent efgartigimod and ofatumumab. The report expands the clinical spectrum of neurexin-3α encephalitis to include choreiform movements and highlights tissue-based assay for diagnosis when conventional screening is negative.

papers.title: Parathyroid Storm Secondary to a Parathyroid Adenoma Presenting With Recurrent Generalised Tonic-Clonic Seizures and Refractory Hypercalcaemia: A Case Report.
papers.summary: Reported a 70-year-old woman with primary hyperparathyroidism who presented with parathyroid storm, severe hypercalcaemia (corrected calcium 4.14 mmol/L), and recurrent generalized tonic-clonic seizures refractory to multimodal medical therapy. Urgent parathyroidectomy produced sustained normalization of serum calcium and cessation of seizures, with histopathology confirming a benign parathyroid adenoma.

papers.title: A SynNotch-PiggyBac gene circuit for inflammation-responsive IL-10 delivery in Alzheimer's disease: a hypothesis and design framework.
papers.summary: Proposes a falsifiable hypothesis and design framework for inflammation-gated IL-10 delivery in Alzheimer's disease using a SynNotch-PiggyBac gene circuit delivered by AAV to astrocytes, with IL-10 transcription triggered by membrane-bound TNF-alpha on activated microglia. Provides a quantitative packaging analysis requiring a compacted vector, identifies three unvalidated assumptions (nonexistent recognition domain, unmeasured ligand surface density, soluble TNF-alpha as competitive inhibitor), and reports a simulated EEG workflow yielding an estimated need for roughly 11 animals per group.

papers.title: Refractory Multivessel Coronary Artery Spasm Unresponsive to Renal Sympathetic Denervation, with Recurrent Transient ST-Segment Elevation and an Episode of Accelerated Idioventricular Rhythm: A Case Report.
papers.summary: Case report of a 53-year-old man with refractory multivessel coronary artery spasm causing recurrent transient ST-segment elevation and a self-terminating accelerated idioventricular rhythm despite dual calcium channel blockade, nitrates, and statin therapy. Radiofrequency renal sympathetic denervation was performed off-label but at six months symptoms and admissions were unchanged, a negative observation adding to limited evidence on autonomic modulation in refractory vasospastic angina.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
